solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Officer's plan again to retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to plan again is to draw up once more

explanation.surface: An officer decides to scrap the plan and fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay: REDRAW backwards is WARDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A warder is a prison guard, one of the uniformed officers who keep order inside a jail.

clue.text: Pole's few lines of poetry

parts.note: read loosely as the article 'an', a single item
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A Polish poet dashes off a few lines of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with a capital suggests a Polish person; it is an electrical pole. 'Few lines of poetry' is simply 'an ode' read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode of a battery or cell, one of its two electrical terminals.

clue.text: Sure to be upset following party conversation

indicators.note: coming after something places this part second in the answer

parts.note: a disco is a dancing party

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a party is bound to take offence at what is being said.
explanation.walkthrough: Though 'Sure' comes first in the clue, 'following' puts its rearranged letters after DISCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal spoken or written exchange, so it serves as a more elevated synonym for talk between people.

clue.text: Spoke favouring reform — not Conservative

indicators.note: 'not' says a letter is absent, so it must be taken out

parts.note: a radical wants sweeping change
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone addressed the meeting in favour of change, and they were no Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past tense of speak; it is the noun, a wheel spoke. Removing the C from RADICAL leaves RADIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial is a line running out from a centre, exactly what a wheel's spoke does between hub and rim.

clue.text: Tribe has bewildered language expert

indicators.note: someone bewildered is confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribe is baffled by a visiting linguist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like a verb in the surface but gives three of the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebraist is a scholar of the Hebrew language, a specialist in one particular ancient tongue.

clue.text: Several faiths TV represented in a religious celebration

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in another form, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A television broadcast shows several faiths taking part in a religious service.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals TV look like an abbreviation but are just two more letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest festival is a church service of thanksgiving for the gathered crops, held in autumn.

clue.text: Short chum sits on meadow, squashing one plant

indicators.note: to squash is to press something inside, so one piece is held within another
something short is cut down, so the final letter goes
in a down answer, sitting on something means coming above it

parts.note: a buddy is a friend
lea is a poetic word for a meadow
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A little friend sits in a field and crushes a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims a whole word, not a letter from the front; lea is a poetic meadow found mostly in crosswords and old verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia is a flowering shrub, often called the butterfly bush, so it is a garden plant.

clue.text: Strong tastes, first to last, creating uncomfortable feeling

indicators.note: the leading letter moves round to the end, the rest staying in order

parts.note: tangs are sharp flavours

explanation.surface: Eating sharp flavours from start to finish leaves you queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the T of TANGS to the back and ANGST appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a deep unease or dread, an anxious state of mind rather than a physical discomfort.

clue.text: Trader giving one artist supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, bending freely, so the letters are flexibly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper provides materials to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as the noun for provisions; it is the adverb from supple. The surface seems to describe what this trader sells.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shopkeeper selling paper, pens and office goods, so a kind of retail trader.

clue.text: Looked at team getting embarrassed after trick

indicators.note: coming after something places the rest behind the first part

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a side is a sports team
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A team was scrutinised and left blushing after a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After trick' means the trick comes first in the answer, even though it is the last word of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to think about or examine it, so looked at in the sense of weighed up.

clue.text: Island for the nobs featured in back issue of periodical

indicators.note: going back means running from end to start
to feature in something is to be included within it

parts.note: a single issue of a periodical is a magazine, shortened
U means upper-class, the style of the nobs

explanation.surface: An exclusive island resort appears in an old issue of a glossy magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is an old convention from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U; nobs are posh people.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is a Pacific island, a United States territory in the Mariana chain.

clue.text: Reduce something bloody, having got back in time

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside another

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: going back means running from end to start

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

explanation.surface: Cut down something gory, having returned in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The sense of the definition is the old one of detracting from something, rarer today than the adjective derogatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To derogate from something is to detract from or lessen its value or authority, hence to diminish it.

clue.text: Endless chatter around a fellow's clubs

indicators.note: turning around sends the letters back the other way
without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: chatter is idle talk
what belongs to a fellow is his

explanation.surface: Nonstop gossip surrounds a man's golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal but here it turns the shortened word back to front. Lathis come from Indian English.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick used as a weapon by Indian police, so lathis are cudgels.

clue.text: Sheep runs that may hold water

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Sheep pastures that might retain rainwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheep runs' reads as grazing land; it splits into a sheep and the letter for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug with a wide mouth, traditionally used to carry washing water.

clue.text: With something large in the environment, lose out completely

indicators.note: an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a whale is a famously large creature

indicators.note: 'out' suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: With something huge in the ecosystem, you lose out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Environment' sounds ecological, fitting a sea creature, but it only means surrounding; 'With' is just a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale as an adverb means on a large scale, indiscriminately, so in total and without exception.

clue.text: This person is probing your old-fashioned food content

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so one piece enters another

parts.note: thine is archaic for your
the setter speaking of themself: I am

explanation.surface: Someone inspects what your outdated diet contains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter, so I AM goes inside THINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamine is vitamin B1, a nutrient present in cereals, pork and pulses, so part of what food contains.

clue.text: Resolved to restrict cold with health-giving ingredients

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: a dispute that is resolved has been mediated
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Determined to limit a chill with healing ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as determined; it is settled, as by a go-between. C goes inside MEDIATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicated describes a product containing a drug or remedy, as in medicated shampoo or sweets.

clue.text: Inscribed within church window maybe see knight

indicators.note: something inscribed within is written inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a lancet is a tall pointed window, one kind found in churches
lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: Engraved inside a church window, perhaps, you can see a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags that a lancet is just one example of a church window.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the most famous of King Arthur's Knights of the Round Table.

clue.text: Poet's line, one on compassion

indicators.note: placed on another part, this one follows it in an across answer

parts.note: love in the sense of charity, caring for others
L is the abbreviation for line
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A poet writes a line on the theme of compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line, one' form a pair that goes on (after) the compassion word in an across entry, not before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was a seventeenth-century English Cavalier poet, known for 'To Althea, from Prison'.

clue.text: Bed or mattress? It may be found in here

definitions.text: Bed or mattress? It may be found in here

indicators.note: something found in a phrase is sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a bed or a mattress belongs in a certain room.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: the answer is hidden in the first three words, and a dormitory is where beds and mattresses are found.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorm, short for dormitory, is a sleeping room full of beds, as in a school or hostel.

clue.text: Love appearing in underwear in funny shows

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be inside it

parts.note: pants is British for underpants
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Romance in one's underwear makes for comic entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantos are pantomimes, British Christmas stage comedies full of slapstick and cross-dressing, where a romance in underwear would fit well.
explanation.definitionFit: A panto is a comic family stage show, so the plural stands for a set of funny performances.

clue.text: Affected by bugs, get cold after first day of month

indicators.note: coming after something places this part at the end

parts.note: the first of September, written with a Roman numeral
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Plagued by insects, you catch a chill as the month begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First day of month' is one particular day, Sept I, rather than an initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic means infected, as a wound becomes when bacteria multiply in it; bugs here are germs.

clue.text: Traffic needs to speed up heading for Edinburgh

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading bottom to top

parts.note: to dart is to move fast

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the city's opening letter

explanation.surface: Vehicles need to go faster on the road into Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' reads as cars on the road; it is the verb or noun for dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means commerce or dealing, especially illicit, so trade is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Melting tarmac starts to restrict some vehicles

indicators.note: melting things lose their shape, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Tarmac softening in the heat begins to hold up some traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' reads as part of the definition in the surface, but it is the second word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramcars are the individual carriages of a tramway, passenger vehicles running on rails through streets.

clue.text: Cheats and criminals caught out

indicators.note: 'out' means excluded, so a letter is removed

parts.note: crooks are villains
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Cheats and criminals get caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught out' is a cricket dismissal in the surface; here it means remove the C from CROOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle them, and a rook is a swindler, especially at cards.

clue.text: Magical power of weaver in story spoken of

indicators.note: what is spoken of is said out loud, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: Silas Marner is the weaver in George Eliot's novel

explanation.surface: A weaver in a tale is said to have supernatural powers.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the R in Marner is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mana is a Polynesian word for supernatural force or authority, now common in fantasy games as magic energy.

clue.text: Priest and French actor performing? It's uplifting

parts.note: Levi was the ancestor of Israel's priestly tribe
Jacques Tati, French comic actor of Monsieur Hulot
on stage means performing

explanation.surface: A priest and a French comedian put on a show, and it cheers everyone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' reads as inspiring; taken literally it is rising into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Levitation is rising or floating in the air without support, so it is literally lifting upward.

clue.text: Base established — cycle around it?

indicators.note: to go around is to encircle, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: to pedal is to ride a bike
est. is the abbreviation for established

explanation.surface: A base has been set up; should you ride your bike round it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to 'established', telling you which word the cycling goes around.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the supporting foot on which a statue or column stands, its base.

clue.text: Perversion is admitted by unfortunate male

indicators.note: to be admitted is to be let inside, so one piece enters another

parts.note: sad in the sense of regrettable
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A wretched man confesses to a perversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' appears as a verb in the surface but is simply two letters taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is deriving pleasure from inflicting pain, classed as a sexual perversion.
